items.title: Fighter scale is too small with excessive dead mat space
items.what: In all portrait gameplay screens (e.g., screenshots 3, 4, 14, 17), the fighters occupy only ~20% of the vertical viewport in the center, leaving a large expanse of empty tatami mat below them and empty shoji panels above.
items.why: On a 390x844 phone screen, the photoreal facial likenesses and subtle martial arts wind-up cues become tiny and difficult to read quickly during high-speed exchanges.
items.how: Tighten the 3D camera framing by lowering camera distance on Z and adjusting Y target so fighter sprites occupy roughly 35-40% of the active combat viewport height above the joystick controls.

items.title: Persistent control cheat sheet clutters active combat area
items.what: A prominent dark rounded box listing 'STANCE' and 'TECHNIQUE' directional legends sits continuously right beneath the fighters and above the thumbsticks during live rounds (screenshots 3, 4, 10, 11, 14, 17).
items.why: It acts as visual clutter directly inside the primary eye-tracking zone between the fighters' feet and the controls, distracting during fast matches.
items.how: Fade this cheat-sheet panel out automatically after the match countdown completes (or upon first joystick touch), keeping it accessible only via the top 'MOVES' modal.

items.title: Half-point stacked fraction misaligns HUD and victory screen text
items.what: In the top HUD (screenshots 12, 16, 17) and the win screen (screenshot 8), the half-point score displays as an unaligned vertical fraction stack that breaks the baseline of opponent scores and results in awkward numeric overlap (e.g., '0 - 2 1/2' in screenshot 8).
items.why: The broken typographic baseline makes fast score checks during a 30-second round visually confusing and looks unpolished on the final results card.
items.how: Format scores using inline glyphs (e.g., '1.5' or '1½') with fixed baseline heights, or render point indicators as discrete visual karate point pips/badges under the competitor names.

items.title: Soft diffuse foot shadows fail to ground the fighter sprites
items.what: Under the fighters' bare feet (seen in screenshots 3, 10, 14, 17), contact shadows are soft, generic circular gradients that do not conform to the stance or sole contact points.
items.why: Because the fighters are photorealistic 2D cutouts positioned in a 3D scene, diffuse blob shadows cause them to look detached and float above the tatami floor.
items.how: Implement tight, higher-opacity ambient occlusion contact shadows directly under the heel and ball of each grounded foot sprite, fading into the broader soft floor shadow.

items.title: Modal overlays have inconsistent sheet heights and clipped scroll content
items.what: The Settings modal (screenshots 7, 13) terminates abruptly mid-screen revealing fighter torsos underneath, while the Techniques modal (screenshot 6) cuts off bottom move entries ('Roundhouse Kick') without clear scroll bounding.
items.why: On mobile devices, half-height non-docked modals look disjointed and risk clipping critical gameplay input reference data.
items.how: Convert modals into standard mobile bottom sheets or full-height overlay drawers with an explicit sticky header/close button and a scrollable viewport container with bottom padding.
